why: The week's honest output is 7 more strangers and three instruments. Sessions read 130 against 50 in the file's own previous window, but composition kills the headline: Direct 94 sessions from 20 users (4.7 each) and github.com 9 from 1 user are 103 of 130 sessions — us. The external audience is 26 sessions / 19 users: google 9 (all brand, all landing on '/'), facebook.com 6 (the same single share, unchanged since 2026-11-07), bitcointalk.org 5 (the 2026-11-12 forum post), t.co 3, x 2, chatgpt.com 1. Test: 26 is the number the plan must beat on 2026-11-24, and if it falls back to 19 the 'growth' was one forum bump.

Indexation is not a crawl-budget problem any more — it is a standing problem, and the evidence is now symmetrical across two engines. Google crawled /articles and /articles/rupl on 2026-11-15 and the redesigned pillar on 2026-11-13, and indexed none; Bing crawled 15 of 21 URLs including '/' on 2026-11-15T23:38:24Z and kept none, six days after all 21 were submitted. Twelve readings at 1/21. The only external signal the domain has is one directory link (lopp.net, merged 2026-11-07) which produced 0 sessions in 9 days and one crawl that arrived 48 seconds after our own Request Indexing. Test: `indexed` 2/21 by 2026-11-28, else the review writes 'authority hypothesis falsified for one followed link' and the plan says a second destination is the whole question — as `lopp-link-effect` is now closed saying.

Non-brand clicks cannot move and 25 readings of proposing snippets proved it: positions4to20 = 0, one non-brand impression at position 38, one page with impressions, and 20 of 21 URLs unserved. This is arithmetic, not a title. The only thing that can put a non-brand query in front of a stranger in the next 13 days is a referral — a forum bump, an X reply, an AI citation — and those click through to pages that Google has never indexed. Test: the first non-brand click can only appear after a URL answering a non-brand query is indexed; no mandate may propose copy work while `indexed` < 5, and today's floor line prints exactly that.

The binding constraint is the owner's send rate, and it is now measured per channel: 13 asks handed over since 2026-10-27, 3 sent, and the one that was sent by hand is the only asked channel that has produced a session (bitcointalk.org 37 reads -> 5 sessions / 2 users, 13.5% per read, against X's 5 sessions from ~316 views, 1.6%). Four asks handed over between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-13 were all unsent today and two lapsed. Worse, the ledger re-issued `github-awesome-blockchain-line-1124` on 2026-11-10 against a destination STATUS.md had withdrawn on 2026-11-04, so the 'live ask' could never converge. Test: the next review reads STATUS.md's sent column and nothing else; if the single live ask is unsent on 2026-11-18, the ask loop stops being the plan and the review says in one line that growth is owner-blocked.

The strategic fact nobody has written down: the site's only live hook is a countdown, and it is worth zero on 2026-11-30. The 2026-11-12 BitcoinTalk topic — the one public act that produced strangers — promises in public that 'on Nov 29, 2026 the rule opens a public $10,000 paper buy, tracked daily to the exit (T+500, currently around Aug 2029). It is a live record, not a forecast.' Nothing implements it: `grep -rin paper src/` returns no page, and the phrase does not appear anywhere in BTC500_GROWTH.md or GROWTH_PROMPT.md. A visitor who arrives on 29 November lands on a page whose central promise is a countdown that has just run out. Test: the record must serve 200 by 2026-11-19 and open with an entry price on 2026-11-29; if it does not, the buy window arrives with a broken public promise and that is the site's result for Q4.

The freeze has become the failure it was written to prevent. It was set on 2026-10-30 to stop unmeasurable content churn, with a stated lift condition: one GA4 referral session from a domain other than github.com. That condition is met twice over (bitcointalk.org 1/1 in the window ending 2026-11-13, 5/2 in the window ending 2026-11-15), and 17 days of total freeze have produced 0 indexed pages, 0 non-brand clicks, 0 new referring domains and 0 site lines since 2026-11-12. Continuing to forbid every site change while the only live hook expires in 13 days is repetition with a rule attached. Test: `indexed` or the external audience must move by 2026-11-29, or the partial lift is reversed and the plan says the site's problem is not in the repository.

The review machinery lost 2026-11-15 and it is not the first time: verdict-invalid on 2026-10-31, 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-15, all three because the run wrote `generated` as the previous day, and two of the three because a Sunday deep run claimed `mode: daily`. So there has been no deep review — no competitor pass, no backlog rescore — since 2026-11-01, during exactly the three weeks this review says the strategy was wrong. Test: the next Sunday (2026-11-22) must produce a valid `deep` file; if it does not, the guard moves from the prompt to the runner and the owner mandate is restated with that evidence.
